title: Unify assistive density, microcopy and validation affordances across form components
creator: Marta Lopez
description: Rationalize how help text, error text, and character/affix affordances render across text fields, selects, toggles and compound inputs at both default and compact densities. Deliver a set of token mappings, updated component specs, and migration notes for the component library and docs.
background: Over the last two quarters multiple quick fixes were applied to individual form components to address specific product needs (compact density, error compacting, prefix/suffix layout). This introduced inconsistent spacing, contrast and assistive behaviour between components and across densities. PMs and engineers observe UX regressions in mobile/tablet flows and we have repeated accessibility support requests about screen reader ordering for helper vs. error messages.
scope:
- Define canonical token mappings for: helper text size/line-height, error text weight/contrast, gap between field and helper row, prefix/suffix affinity spacing, and inline validation icon sizing for both default and compact densities.
- Update component specs for TextField, Select, Textarea, Toggle, MultiField (chip-style inputs) to adopt the tokens and clarified DOM order for assistive text.
- Produce accessible examples (screen reader order, aria-live usage for validation) and add to docs.
- Provide migration guidance for existing product screens and a small PR template for component owners.
out_of_scope:
- Rewriting the form validation engine or server-side validation paths.
- Changing color palette tokens beyond contrast fixes required for errors.
- Replacing third-party select library — we'll adapt spec within current implementation constraints.
design_goals: Consistent visual rhythm for helper/error rows across densities and breakpoints
Predictable DOM order and aria patterns so screen readers announce errors before helpers when present
Minimal breaking changes for consuming teams, with clear migration notes and deprecation windows
Maintain or improve color contrast to meet WCAG 2.1 AA for validation states
Support i18n line-wrapping and RTL layout for helper/error rows
decisions: Helper/error rows will live in the DOM immediately after the input element to preserve logical reading order (input -> error -> helper).
Introduce two token groups: form.helper.* and form.validation.* with explicit density suffixes (.default / .compact).
Error messages will use a semibold weight, a single error icon size across densities, and a 12px minimum touch/visual gap from the input in compact mode.
ARIA: validation messages will use aria-live='assertive' only when a programmatic validation occurs; otherwise aria-describedby links will be used for static helper text.
For selects using portal overlays, helper text will remain adjacent to the trigger; dropdown-specific hints should be in the overlay footer and documented as separate tokens.
tradeoffs: DOM reorder (error before helper) could briefly break custom consumers relying on previous sibling selectors; mitigation: provide migration guide and CSS helper classes.
Using aria-live selectively reduces noisy announcements but requires engineering discipline to mark programmatic validations appropriately.

Keeping a single error icon size simplifies asset management but may feel visually dense on very large input sizes; we will add a visual guideline for oversized fields instead of adding more token complexity.
tasks: Audit current components for helper/error differences (DES audit spreadsheet link in links).
Define token values and publish to token repo (token PR).
Update TextField spec and Figma components, include compact and default variants.
Update Select and Toggle specs to match helper/error pattern; create overlay-specific guidance for selects.
Create accessible example pages (screen reader walkthroughs) and automated axe checks in the docs site.
Write migration notes and announce deprecation plan to component owners.
Ship small library patch with opt-in flags for teams to test before full rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Token PR merged and released to design tokens package with versioned changelog entry.
Updated component specs in the design system docs with examples for default and compact densities.
At least three product screens updated by owning teams using the new tokens as part of the rollout trial.
Accessibility checklist items validated: screen reader reads error before helper when errors present; aria-describedby links work for static helpers; WCAG contrast for error text >= AA.
Migration guide published and at least one consuming engineering team signs off on feasibility.
No new visual regressions on high-traffic pages as measured by component snapshot diff (visual regression threshold defined in PR).
